syllabus_excerpts.module_name: Module 1 – Introduction to DBMS & Relational Model
syllabus_excerpts.text: Database system concepts and architecture; Data models, schemas, and instances; Three-schema architecture and data independence; Entity-Relationship (ER) model: entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality ratios, and ER-to-relational mapping; Relational Model constraints: domain constraints, key constraints, entity integrity, and referential integrity.

Relational algebra operations: select, project, join, set operations, division; SQL: DDL, DML, DCL commands, complex queries, nested subqueries, views, triggers, and assertion constraints; Aggregate functions, group by and having clauses.

Functional dependencies and inference rules (Armstrong axioms); Normal forms based on primary keys: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF; Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF); Multivalued dependencies and 4NF; Lossless-join decomposition and dependency preservation properties.

Transaction concepts, ACID properties, transaction state diagram; Serializability: conflict serializability and view serializability; Concurrency control protocols: two-phase locking (2PL) protocol, strict 2PL, timestamp ordering protocol; Deadlock detection, prevention, and recovery mechanisms.

File organization, ordered indices, primary and secondary indices; B-Tree and B+ Tree index structures; Hashing techniques: static and dynamic hashing; Query evaluation steps, cost estimation, and basic query optimization heuristics.

labeled_questions.question_text: Explain the advantages of database normalization with a suitable real-world example.
Describe why normalization is necessary in relational database design and illustrate with an example.
Consider two concurrent transactions T1 and T2. Demonstrate how the Two-Phase Locking (2PL) protocol ensures conflict serializability.
Illustrate with schedules how 2PL protocol guarantees serializability for concurrent transactions.
Differentiate between WHERE and HAVING clauses in SQL with brief syntax.
Calculate the maximum number of record pointers in a B+ tree of order 4 and height 3.

labeled_pairs.reason: Both ask for advantages/necessity of normalization with an example in different wording.
Both ask how 2PL guarantees serializability for concurrent schedules.
Different modules: Normalization vs Concurrency Control.
Completely distinct topics: SQL syntax vs B+ tree calculation.
